candidate.paper: Seed-Prover 1.5: Mastering Undergraduate-Level Theorem Proving via Learning from Experience

primary_paper_verification.agentic_environment: The same autoregressive prover interleaves natural-language reasoning with Lean verification, Mathlib semantic search and Python execution. Multiple tool calls can occur within one turn, with no fixed ordering imposed.
primary_paper_verification.post_training: The paper states that the agentic prover is post-trained with VAPO/PPO-style tool-integrated reinforcement learning over trajectories containing interleaved tool calls and tool responses.
primary_paper_verification.terminal_reward: Outcome reward is +1 when a completed proof is verified by Lean and -1 otherwise.
primary_paper_verification.training_behavior_metrics: During RL training, average function calls fall from roughly 15-16 to roughly 10 and average total sequence length from roughly 29k to roughly 17k tokens while the reported training/test reasoning score rises.
primary_paper_verification.adaptive_search_behavior: At inference, the paper reports approximately 10 Mathlib-search calls per Fate-H trajectory versus 1-2 on Putnam, and fewer search calls at later checkpoints while performance continues improving.
primary_paper_verification.full_system_distinction: The official README/paper headline values 88% PutnamBench, 80% Fate-H and 33% Fate-X refer to the full Seed-Prover 1.5 system/workflow, not the agentic-prover-only Table-1 setting above.

claim_assessment.broad_claim: A formal-proof agent exists in which a full-model outer interaction policy is trained from sequential terminal verifier-grounded reward rather than only next-tactic imitation.
claim_assessment.causal_scope: The declining tool-call/sequence-length metrics and dataset-dependent search distributions are direct behavioral observations during/after RL training, but the paper does not provide a matched controller-only ablation that isolates tool-routing skill from simultaneous improvements in proof reasoning/model capability. They therefore do not identify the causal contribution of routing alone.
narrow_controller_gap_details: The policy is a large free-form autoregressive model, not a separately factored compact typed meta-controller.
No explicit hard legal-action mask or action propensity log/OPE protocol is reported for the high-level tool-selection policy.
The reward is binary proof success/failure and contains no explicit token, dollar, Lean-time, wall-clock or worker-slot cost term.
No matched experiment holds proof-generation capability fixed while changing only a compact high-level controller.

public_artifact_verification.artifact_scope: The pinned SeedProver-1.5 directory publishes the report and proof artifacts but does not expose the agentic-RL trainer/controller implementation or trajectory dataset. This supports use as a scientific capability baseline, not as a drop-in replayable controller benchmark from that directory alone. Other repository directories are outside this artifact-inventory claim and were not treated as equivalent to the 1.5 release.

scope_guard: Evidence applies to Seed-Prover 1.5's reported Lean proving environments, training/evaluation settings and pinned public 1.5 release directory. Do not generalize binary terminal reward as cost-optimal routing, do not equate full-system headline scores with the agentic-prover-only Table-1 baseline, and do not infer a compact auditable controller from a full-model agentic policy.
exact_next_action: Continue C11 rotation to an under-audited candidate with released raw quantitative artifacts; prefer a claim where exact numbers can be independently recomputed or replayed rather than only source-text corroborated.
